ports.note: A table in, a table of estimates out: one row per reported term with its ratio, interval limits and p. The design port is optional. A declared design decides the measure: a rate ratio under cohort and ecological designs, an odds ratio wherever the two-by-two allows one (a prevalence odds ratio under a cross-sectional design); anything else stops the step, saying why.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no mapping to an external vocabulary -- not meaning the terms are undeclared. fw:RegressionModel is declared in ontology/runtime.ttl, and each coefficient is an fw:EpiEstimate, the class the two-by-two uses. The receipt states the family, the outcome, the exposure and every adjustment with how it entered the model, strata, an offset, the error method, rows used and left out, strata used and dropped, and for each estimate its name, term, interval method and level. fw:RegressionModelShape and fw:EpiEstimateShape in ontology/shapes/quality-and-design.ttl hold the receipt to that. Experiment 176.

changes.description: The Preview reports EACH MODEL'S own sample, and reads a cell as the fit reads it. With several exposure columns the run fits one model each, every model leaving out only the rows its own variables are missing on; this reported the first exposure's as though it were all of them (4 of 4 usable where the second had 2). `exposureColumnsOf` and `modelParams` moved to regression-sample.ts beside the row rule, so the Preview enumerates the models the run will fit. And the case summary now trims as the exclusion rule does: a whitespace-padded `yes` was admitted as a case by one and counted as a non-case by the other, two normalizations inside one Preview disagreeing about the same cell.

evidence.note:
Kernel unit tests: a two-by-two as logistic regression gives its odds ratio and Woolf's standard error; an unadjusted Poisson model gives the rate ratio; absorbed strata give the coefficients of the model with stratum indicators. Published figures reproduced on the authors' own data: NYC ozone 1.0609 per 10 ppb, coefficient and HAC standard error equal to the authors' archived R result to 12 significant figures; Salmonella Galia melon adjusted for age group (7 groups) and sex, 96 (15-2067) and 18 (4.6-101) against the published 96 (15-2100) and 18 (4.6-100). Nothing here establishes that a model is well specified. One model per exposure column (0.4.0): each model's estimates equal the single model fitted on that column alone, and each uses exactly the rows its own column has a value on, never the rows common to all (tests/regression-per-exposure.test.mjs, synthetic data). Not yet compared with Validation Lab checks 36 and 37 or the 2010-2025 figures in experiment 182. 0.6.0: tests/regression-per-exposure.browser.mjs and tests/salmonella-from-scratch.browser.mjs set the model in Configure… and check the Inspector's sentence; Chromium. tests/regression-per-exposure.test.mjs: fitted one at a time, the models equal those fitted together, each announced before it is fitted.

THE PREVIEW (2026-11-25). Browser tested on Chromium: tests/settings-previews.browser.mjs asserts 8 of 10 rows complete where two are empty in the exposure, the case split, and the exposure's smallest level. NOT established: that the rows counted here are exactly the rows the fit uses, which would need a test holding both.

THE SHARED RULE (2026-11-25). tests/regression.test.mjs and tests/regression-per-exposure.test.mjs pass unchanged across the extraction, so the fit's sample is the same as before; tests/settings-previews.browser.mjs asserts the Preview's count and its reasons on Chromium. NOT established: that the two agree on every shape, which would need a test fitting and previewing the same table.

PER-MODEL SAMPLE AND SHARED NORMALIZATION (2026-11-26). tests/settings-previews.browser.mjs asserts two exposures with different samples and a padded case value, on Chromium; the fit's own tests pass unchanged across moving the two helpers. Found in review of 0.198.0.
